subject.title: feat(plugins): upgrade llm_input/llm_output hooks from fire-and-forget to modifying

question: Should modifying LLM interception use separate or versioned hooks, or should OpenClaw intentionally replace the shipped observer-only `llm_input` and `llm_output` contract?
rationale: This choice permanently changes a public plugin API's timing, authority, availability, failure behavior, and cross-runner guarantees; implementation review cannot safely choose that product contract.

options.title: Add separate modifying hooks
options.body: Preserve the existing fire-and-forget observers and add clearly named modifiers implemented consistently across every runner and output boundary.

options.title: Version the existing hooks
options.body: Adopt modifying semantics only with explicit migration guidance, compatibility coverage, and complete runner enforcement.

options.title: Keep observation only
options.body: Decline model interception in core and retain the current observer contract.

recommendation.title: Add separate modifying hooks
recommendation.body: Preserve the existing fire-and-forget observers and add clearly named modifiers implemented consistently across every runner and output boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and validated the shipped observer contract, making them the strongest evidenced routing candidate for whether that contract may change.
